what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat low testosterone levels in adult men, a condition sometimes called hypogonadism or 'low T.' Your body needs testosterone for normal sexual function, energy, mood, muscle strength, and bone health. This medicine replaces or adds to the testosterone your body is not making enough of on its own.
how_to_take: How you take this medicine depends on the form your doctor prescribed. CAPSULES (Jatenzo, Kyzatrex, Tlando): Swallow the capsules whole with food — do not crush, chew, or break them. Take them with a meal to help your body absorb the medicine properly. INJECTION (Aveed): This shot is given by a healthcare provider into a muscle (usually the buttock) in a clinic or doctor's office. You will NOT give this injection to yourself at home. You must stay at the clinic for at least 30 minutes after each injection so staff can watch for any serious reactions.
dosing: CAPSULES: The usual starting dose is 2 capsules taken twice a day with food (morning and evening meals). Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your testosterone blood levels. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. INJECTION: The first two injections are given 4 weeks apart. After that, injections are given every 10 weeks. Your doctor will check your testosterone levels and may adjust how often you receive injections.
missed_dose: CAPSULES: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember WITH food. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. INJECTION: Since your injection is given by a healthcare provider, call your doctor's office as soon as possible to reschedule your appointment if you miss it. Try not to delay your injection for too long.
storage: CAPSULES: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep out of reach of children and pets. INJECTION: This medicine is stored and handled by your healthcare provider's office. You do not need to store it at home. All forms: Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about drug take-back programs in your area.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice while taking the capsule form, as it may affect how the medicine works in your body. Avoid sharing this medicine with anyone else — it is prescribed only for you. Women and children should avoid skin contact with areas where testosterone has been applied (if using other forms). Avoid activities that require you to be alert if you feel dizzy after your injection. Tell your doctor before taking blood thinners (like warfarin), insulin, or medicines for diabetes, as testosterone may affect how these work. Avoid using testosterone if you have or have had prostate cancer or breast cancer.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing up blood (signs of a blood clot or serious lung reaction — this can happen after an injection); signs of a stroke such as sudden numbness, severe headache, vision changes, or trouble speaking; painful or prolonged erections lasting more than 4 hours (priapism); swelling in your legs or ankles; changes in your mood such as increased aggression, depression, or thoughts of self-harm; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; sleep apnea symptoms such as loud snoring or gasping for air while sleeping; increased acne, hair loss, or breast tenderness or swelling. Also call your doctor if you notice any lumps or changes in your testicles, or if you and your partner are trying to have children, as testosterone therapy can reduce sperm count.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvements — such as better energy, mood, and sex drive — within a few weeks of starting treatment. Full benefits, including improved muscle strength and bone density, may take 3 to 6 months or longer. Your doctor will check your testosterone blood levels regularly to make sure the medicine is working and that your levels are in a safe range. Be patient and keep all of your follow-up appointments.
special_populations: OLDER MEN (65 and older): Use with caution. Older men may be at higher risk for side effects such as fluid retention and heart or prostate problems. Your doctor will monitor you closely. MEN WITH HEART OR KIDNEY DISEASE: Tell your doctor about any heart, kidney, or liver problems before starting this medicine, as it may cause fluid retention and could worsen these conditions. MEN WITH SLEEP APNEA: Testosterone can make sleep apnea worse. Talk to your doctor if you snore heavily or have been told you stop breathing during sleep. WOMEN AND CHILDREN: This medicine is NOT approved for use in women or children. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant must not handle this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. FERTILITY: This medicine can lower sperm production and reduce fertility. If you are planning to have children, discuss other treatment options with your doctor before starting testosterone therapy.
